title: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head V (Ministry of Trade and Industry)

sections.label: Budget cut motion on economy
sections.summary: A motion to reduce Head V of the Estimates by $100, noting the economy faces deep structural change in the global order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head V of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, our economy today is less about weathering cyclical volatility and more about navigating deep structural change in the global order.

sections.label: Singapore's three-part economic strategy
sections.summary: Singapore's strategy must strengthen business resilience, move into higher-value growth areas and translate growth into quality jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In this environment, Singapore’s strategy must do three things simultaneously: strengthen business resilience, move decisively into higher-value growth areas and translate growth into quality jobs for Singaporeans.

sections.label: Wage co-funding and counter-cyclical support
sections.summary: Asks whether wage and training co-funding for job redesign can be strengthened and whether a counter-cyclical accelerator should be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can we strengthen wage and training co-funding for job redesign, particularly in sectors exposed to global competition, so that firms upgrade jobs rather than displace workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And given the increasingly volatile global environment, should we consider a counter-cyclical accelerator, pre-approved support that can be activated quickly during downturns, so that firms and workers receive timely assistance without delays?

sections.label: Greener energy transition
sections.summary: As a resource-scarce country, Singapore must accelerate its transition to greener energy to reduce vulnerability to global price shocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As a resource-scarce country, we must accelerate our transition to greener energy to reduce vulnerability to global price shocks, especially in an era of heightened geopolitical fragmentation.

sections.label: Decarbonisation jobs and energy affordability
sections.summary: Asks about projected job creation from decarbonisation and how sustainability ambitions can be met while keeping energy reliable and affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What is the projected job creation from our decarbonisation push, across renewables integration, hydrogen, carbon management and grid resilience?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How do we ensure that our sustainability ambitions are achieved while keeping energy reliable and affordable for households and businesses?

sections.label: Fiscal buffers and capability building
sections.summary: Fiscal discipline and buffers give space to respond to shocks, but long-term competitiveness depends on building, retaining and renewing capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In a more volatile global environment, fiscal discipline and buffers give us the space to respond to shocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But ultimately, our long-term competitiveness will depend on how deeply we build, retain and renew capabilities within our economy.

sections.label: Target for new local companies
sections.summary: MTI could consider setting an ambitious target for new local companies to reach that scale by 2035, so agencies can marshal resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MTI could consider setting an ambitious target for a number of new local companies to reach that scale by 2035 so that all Government agencies can marshal their resources to achieve this.

sections.label: Separate tier for mid-sized companies
sections.summary: MTI could consider adding a separate tier of companies between $100 and $200 million in annual revenue, with slightly lower support than the SME tier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: MTI could consider adding a separate tier of companies between $100 and $200 million in annual revenue, with slightly lower support than the SME tier, so that there is a gentler cliff effect in support levels, which are typically more generous for SMEs.

sections.label: Enterprise Financing Scheme domestic acquisitions support
sections.summary: The Enterprise Financing Scheme supports domestic acquisitions by firms up to $500 million in revenue, but this support lapses in a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Currently, the Enterprise Financing Scheme supports domestic acquisitions undertaken by firms up to $500 million in revenue, but this support lapses in a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This was not mentioned in the Budget Statement.

sections.label: Process duration from referral to Court Order
sections.summary: In recent cases, the process has taken between 28 and 39 months from referral to Court Order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In recent cases, the process has taken between 28 and 39 months from referral to Court Order.

sections.label: CCS administrative enforcement powers for CPFTA
sections.summary: CCS already exercises administrative powers under the Competition Act, and the Government is called on to grant similar powers for CPFTA breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Today, CCS already exercises administrative powers under the Competition Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to grant CCS similar administrative enforcement powers for breaches of the CPFTA.

sections.label: Mandatory cooling-off period for prepayments
sections.summary: In 2025, consumers suffered over $2.7 million in prepayment losses, and the Government is called on to introduce a mandatory cooling-off period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In 2025, consumers suffered over $2.7 million in prepayment losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: When such businesses fail, consumers are left bearing the losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I therefore call on the Government to introduce a mandatory cooling-off period for all businesses that collect significant prepayments.

sections.label: CCS action against brands
sections.summary: CCS took action against Sterra, PRISM+ and COURTS for false claims, fake countdown timers and unsolicited cart additions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In August 2024, CCS took action against Sterra, a water filter brand that falsely claimed that Singapore's tap water was unsafe to drink and sold products marketed as being manufactured in Korea and Singapore when they were in fact manufactured in China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Last December, CCS acted against PRISM+ for fake countdown timers on their website that served no technical function and simply reset to zero; and against COURTS for silently adding unsolicited products to customers' shopping carts.

sections.label: Beauty industry complaints surge
sections.summary: CASE's February 2026 report recorded a 76% surge in beauty industry complaints, with consumers losing over $2.1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: CASE's February 2026 report recorded a 76% surge in beauty industry complaints last year, with consumers losing over $2.1 million.

sections.label: Beauty salon chain complaints
sections.summary: Another chain of beauty salons drew 53 complaints exceeding $980,000 in total.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Another chain of beauty salons – 53 complaints, exceeding $980,000 in total.

sections.label: Hong Kong biomedical listing rules
sections.summary: Hong Kong has pre-commercialisation listing rules for biomedical and specialist technology companies under rules 18A and 18C.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If you look up north, a little bit further, in Hong Kong, they have the pre-commercialisation listing rules for biomedical under the listing 18A rules or the 18C rules, which is specialist technology companies.

sections.label: Segment employment and value added
sections.summary: They provide economic stability and livelihoods, employing 45% of workers but contributing only 11% of nominal value added.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They provide economic stability for the nation and livelihoods for many workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They employ 45% of our workers but contribute only 11% of nominal value added.

sections.label: ASME GDP uplift estimate
sections.summary: ASME estimates a 10% uplift in this segment's value added could add $6.5 billion in annual GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: ASME estimates that a 10% uplift in the value added of this segment could translate to an additional $6.5 billion dollars in annual gross domestic product (GDP), equivalent to more than one percent of growth.

sections.label: Succession planning in SME transformation
sections.summary: Unclear succession and informal governance hinder investment, so the speaker suggests integrating succession planning and family ownership transition into the SME transformation framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Where succession is unclear or governance frameworks remain informal, it becomes difficult to invest in digitalisation, expansion or strategic pivots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: I therefore suggest that our SME transformation framework integrate succession planning and family ownership transition as core components of enterprise upgrading.

sections.label: SMEs employ Singapore workforce
sections.summary: About 70% of Singapore's workforce, approximately 2.5 million people, are employed under SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Chairman, about 70% of our Singapore workforce, approximately 2.5 million people are employed under the SMEs.

sections.label: Integrated AI assistant for Government portals
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether an integrated AI assistant could understand firms' profiles and automatically suggest relevant programmes and schemes on Government portals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: When an SME logs into a Government portal, whether it is for a licence, grant or financing, could there be an integrated AI assistant that understand the firms' profiles and suggest relevant programmes and schemes automatically?

sections.label: Support operating in sync
sections.summary: The question is whether support operates in sync, and this year's Budget provides tax rebates and expansion support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The question is not whether support exists today, but whether it operates in sync.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This year's Budget provide tax rebates and expansion support.

sections.label: Enterprise upgrading and AI adoption
sections.summary: Enterprise upgrading and AI adoption are a matter of national competitiveness, not just for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Chairman, enterprise upgrading and AI adoption are a matter of national competitiveness and not just for SMEs.

sections.label: Narrowing enterprise ecosystem gap
sections.summary: Restricted access and slow digital adoption could create an ecosystem gap, and the speaker suggests offering SMEs a year-long subscription to enterprise AI tools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: They face restricted access on one end and slow digital adoption on the other.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This could create an enterprise ecosystem gap where larger firms surge ahead due to technology and skill, while smaller enterprises struggle to keep up with access, tools and capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan (Sembawang)
sentences.text: One practical way to narrow this gap is to offer SMEs a year-long subscription to enterprise AI tools, similar to the approach I suggested in my muted Ministry of Finance (MOF) cut.

sections.label: Prioritising scalable SMEs
sections.summary: Asks whether SMEs willing and able to scale, innovate and uplift productivity should be prioritised in a resource-constrained environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In a resource-constrained environment, should we more deliberately prioritise SMEs that are willing and able, or potentially able, to scale, to innovate and uplift productivity meaningfully?

sections.label: F&B fragility and SME productivity
sections.summary: Asks whether structural fragility in F&B is being confronted and how SMEs can move beyond digital adoption to measured productivity growth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Are we confronting structural fragility in sectors like F&B, so new entrants can assess their viability more realistically?

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: And most importantly, how do we help SMEs move beyond digital adoption to sustained, measured productivity growth, especially those with intent and potential to compete?

sections.label: SMEs must internationalise
sections.summary: States that Singapore SMEs face operational constraints and transformation pressures, and must internationalise because the domestic market is limited.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Chairman, Singapore SMEs face distinct challenges alongside day‑to‑day operational constraints and pressures to transform, they must internationalise because our domestic market is limited.

sections.label: Targeting grants and tax deductions
sections.summary: Asks how the Government will ensure financial support and tax deduction eligibility criteria are precisely targeted so funds create intended impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Learning from past experiences administering grants and credits, how will the Government ensure that financial support and eligibility criteria for tax deductions are precisely targeted, so that funds are spent effectively to create the intended impact.

sections.label: Support for local retailers' premises
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry can consider measures such as rental relief, tenancy support, landlord incentives and co-investment platforms for local businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry consider targeted measures, such as rental relief schemes, tenancy support for heritage and neighbourhood retailers, incentives for landlords to prioritise local tenants or co‑investment platforms that enable local businesses to secure long‑term premises?

sections.label: Partnerships and FTAs after US tariffs
sections.summary: Says that in light of US tariffs on Singapore, the Ministry should explore partnerships with other nations and additional Free Trade Agreements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azhar Othman (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In light of the tariffs imposed by the US on various countries, including Singapore, it is crucial for the Ministry to explore potential partnerships with other nations and develop additional Free Trade Agreements (FTAs).

sections.label: GNP indicators for overseas value
sections.summary: A suggestion that MTI develop GNP indicators to track value created globally by Singapore and Singaporeans overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We should measure their overseas activity, their value added, to reflect our actual economic network strength.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I suggest that MTI develops GNP indicators to track value created globally by Singapore and Singaporeans overseas.

sections.label: Marketing Johor-Singapore SEZ deployment
sections.summary: A question on how MTI can direct agencies with MFA to market a two-side deployment proposition into the Johor-Singapore SEZ.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We in Singapore capture the trust premium here, while unlocking cost and space constraints that we have right next door as one integrated operating model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, my question is, how can MTI direct EDB, Enterprise Singapore and other economic agencies in coordination with MFA to package and to market a two-side deployment proposition, where inward investors or anchors enter Singapore through Singapore as the trusted gateway and deploy into the Johor-Singapore SEZ?

sections.label: Johor-Singapore SEZ outcome scorecard
sections.summary: A suggestion to publish a Johor-Singapore SEZ outcome scorecard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Suggestion four – publish a Johor-Singapore SEZ outcome scorecard.

sections.label: Trusted place to deploy AI
sections.summary: Singapore's advantage is being the most trusted place to deploy AI, not adopting AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Singapore's advantage is not about adopting AI but being the most trusted place to deploy AI.

sections.label: Four shifts for growing economy
sections.summary: Four shifts are shared for growing the economy in a fragmenting world, covering global value, ecosystems, overseas workforce and AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, going forward, in this very fragmenting world, we need to change the way we look at how we grow our economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I have shared four shifts: from measuring domestic to tracking global value; from individual expansion to ecosystem; from a locally-bound workforce to an overseas one; and finally, AI as trusted infrastructure.

sections.label: SME overseas expansion versus workforce
sections.summary: Four in five Singapore SMEs plan to expand overseas, but only 3.1% of the resident workforce has worked overseas full-time for six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In my Budget speech, I shared that four in five Singapore SMEs plan to expand overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Elysa Chen (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Yet only 3.1% of our resident workforce has worked overseas full-time for at least six months.

sections.label: Internationalisation support by market risk
sections.summary: MTI is asked to consider differentiating internationalisation support by market risk profile, with enhanced guarantees, political risk coverage or risk-sharing in higher-risk corridors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could MTI consider differentiating internationalisation support not only by firm size, but also by market risk profile, with enhanced working capital guarantees, political risk coverage or expanded risk-sharing mechanisms in higher-risk corridors?

sections.label: Consortium-led bids for firms
sections.summary: Encouraging consortium-led bids would let complementary Singapore companies pool capabilities, share risk and compete for projects none could secure alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Encouraging consortium-led bids, enabling firms to "hunt as a pack", would allow complementary Singapore companies to pool capabilities, share risk and compete for projects none could secure alone.

sections.label: Startup SG Equity $1 billion injection
sections.summary: With an additional $1 billion injection into Startup SG Equity, MTI is asked what specific gap is being closed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
sentences.text: With the additional $1 billion injection into our Startup SG Equity, I would like to ask MTI what specific gap we are trying to close?

sections.label: Startup SG Founder first-time founder rule
sections.summary: The member asks about the Startup SG Founder scheme, having heard one founder must be a first-time founder to get it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
sentences.text: Beyond funding, I would like to check on the Startup SG Founder scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
sentences.text: I heard that one of the founders must be a first-time founder to get this scheme.

sections.label: Chief AI officer as a service
sections.summary: The member asks whether a chief AI officer as a service model could be explored to let experienced AI leaders support multiple startups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
sentences.text: Could we explore a chief AI officer as a service model, allowing experienced AI leaders to support multiple startups so that they can deploy AI properly and scale with confidently?

sections.label: Singapore economy grew 5%
sections.summary: Last year Singapore's economy grew by 5%, performing better than expected despite a challenging global environment.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Last year, Singapore's economy grew by 5%, performing better than expected despite a challenging global environment.

sections.label: US tariffs struck down
sections.summary: The US Supreme Court struck down last year's reciprocal tariffs, and the US Administration replaced them with a new Section 122 tariff of 10% for up to 150 days.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The United States (US) Supreme Court has struck down the reciprocal tariffs that were imposed last year and the US Administration has since replaced it with a new Section 122 tariff of 10% for up to 150 days.

sections.label: Strait of Hormuz closed
sections.summary: The Strait of Hormuz, a key shipping route for crude oil and LNG, has been closed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The Strait of Hormuz, which is a key shipping route for crude oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG), has been closed.

sections.label: Economic Strategy Review set up
sections.summary: The Government set up the Economic Strategy Review to reset Singapore's economic strategy and reach the higher end of 2% to 3% GDP trend-growth.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: This is why the Government set up the Economic Strategy Review (ESR) to take a hard, honest look at how Singapore must reset our economic strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will have to work harder and smarter, be creative and take calculated risks, and explore bold solutions to reach the higher end of our GDP trend-growth of 2% to 3% per annum, on average, over the next decade and create good jobs.

sections.label: AI Centres of Excellence support
sections.summary: Over 60 companies have been supported to establish AI Centres of Excellence, and a "Champions of AI" programme will launch later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To date, we have supported over 60 companies to establish AI Centres of Excellence.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: These are in-house teams focussed on developing and deploying AI solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will take this further by launching a "Champions of AI" programme later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Under this programme, we will target a select group of Singapore-based companies with the ambition and commitment to make AI a core driver of productivity, innovation and growth.

sections.label: DBS AI in institutional banking
sections.summary: DBS has deployed AI in institutional banking, reducing processing times for trade documentation by 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: DBS has also deployed AI in institutional banking, reducing processing times for trade documentation by 60%.

sections.label: DBS AI economic value
sections.summary: In 2025 DBS reported about $1 billion in economic value from data analytics, AI and Machine Learning, and AI Missions will start with four sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In 2025, DBS reported that economic value from its data analytics, AI and Machine Learning initiatives achieved a record of approximately $1 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We also want to be an AI leader in the development, testing, deployment and scaling of AI.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will drive AI transformation at the sector level through AI Missions, starting with advanced manufacturing, connectivity, finance and healthcare – sectors where Singapore already has strong foundations.

sections.label: AI Park and Kampong AI
sections.summary: An AI Park and Kampong AI at One-North will be established to bring talent, researchers and resources together for AI excellence.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will also establish an AI Park as a focal point where talent, problem owners, researchers and resources can come together to create synergy and nurture a deep ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We already have Lorong AI; and we will now also build an entire "Kampong" – Kampong AI at One-North. "Kampong AI" will accelerate collaboration and serve as a centre of gravity for AI excellence.

sections.label: Support for overseas ventures
sections.summary: Support will be stepped up for leading companies pursuing significant overseas ventures, especially in developing and emerging markets.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: This will allow them to benefit from the growth of the global economy, while anchoring value, capabilities and leadership functions here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We will step up support for leading companies pursuing significant overseas ventures that may involve higher risks and capital outlay, especially in developing and emerging markets, but which give them a real and lasting foothold in key markets and value chains.

sections.label: Singapore Battery Consortium funding
sections.summary: Industry platforms like the Singapore Battery Consortium bring players together, and NRF funding for the Consortium ends on 31 March.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
sentences.text: Industry platforms, such as the Singapore Battery Consortium, have played a useful role in bringing in together the different players.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
sentences.text: I understand that National Research Foundation's (NRF's) funding for the Consortium will end on 31 March.

sections.label: Natural gas electricity share
sections.summary: Natural gas supplies roughly 95% of Singapore's electricity today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Today, natural gas supplies roughly 95% of our electricity.

sections.label: Shipping route disruption risk
sections.summary: Disruptions to key shipping routes like the Strait of Hormuz could send energy prices soaring.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Disruptions to key shipping routes like the Strait of Hormuz where a large portion of LNG passes could send energy prices soaring.

sections.label: Carbon tax rise
sections.summary: Singapore's carbon tax is expected to rise to signal decarbonisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Singapore's carbon tax is expected to rise to signal decarbonisation.

sections.label: Energy demand and supply diversification
sections.summary: AI data centres, quantum computing, semiconductor fabrication, advanced manufacturing and transport electrification will raise consumption, while imports and solar diversify supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: AI data centres, quantum computing, semiconductor fabrication, advanced manufacturing and transport electrification will significantly increase consumption, while imports and intermittent sources like solar diversify supply.

sections.label: Grid reinforcement and storage investments
sections.summary: It asks what investments are being made in grid reinforcement, storage and system balancing to keep reliability uncompromised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: What investments are we making in grid reinforcement, storage and system balancing to ensure reliability remains uncompromised?

sections.label: Dynamic pricing and emissions factor
sections.summary: It asks whether more dynamic pricing and a time-differentiated grid emissions factor could align demand with peak renewable generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: Could more dynamic pricing better align demand with peak renewable generation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
sentences.text: A time-differentiated grid emissions factor could incentivise load shifting, reduce strain and support decarbonisation.

sections.label: R&D and semiconductor investments
sections.summary: Private sector R&D expenditure was $4.3 billion in 2023, and $800 million will establish the RIE Flagship in Semiconductors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For manufacturing, the annual private sector R&D expenditure in 2023 was $4.3 billion, which is a 54% increase from 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We have built strong R&D capabilities through past RIE investments, and we have anchored a total of more than $30 billion in investments from semiconductor companies, over the past four years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will further invest $800 million to establish the RIE Flagship in Semiconductors, focusing on high-impact technology areas, such as Advanced Packaging and Advanced Photonics, which boost chip performance while cutting power use.

sections.label: NSTIC power electronics investment
sections.summary: The facility is on track to commence operations by 2027, and $60 million will be invested in NSTIC (Power Electronics).

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: It is on track to commence operations by 2027, and companies have shown strong interest in the facility’s collaboration space.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will also invest $60 million in NSTIC (Power Electronics) to strengthen Singapore’s competitiveness in next-generation power electronics.

sections.label: RIE2030 RIS(C) investment
sections.summary: More than $3 billion will be invested in RIS(C) in RIE2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Building on this, we will invest more than $3 billion in RIS(C) in RIE2030.

sections.label: NSAS expected to double in size
sections.summary: From an initial 30 officers from OSTIn, NSAS is expected to double in size over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: From the initial 30 officers from the Office for Space Technology and Industry (OSTIn), NSAS is expected to double in size over the next three years.

sections.label: Solar capacity target raised to three GWp
sections.summary: The 2030 solar target of two GWp was reached last year, so the target is raised to three GWp by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Last year, we reached our 2030 target of two gigawatt-peak (GWp) of installed solar capacity, five years ahead of schedule.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are therefore raising the target to three GWp – an increase of 50% – by 2030, and we aspire to double last year’s achievement within the second half of the 2030s.

sections.label: Conditional Approvals awarded to projects
sections.summary: Around 8.4 gigawatts of Conditional Approvals have been awarded to promising projects to date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To date, we have awarded around 8.4 gigawatts (GW) of Conditional Approvals to promising projects.

sections.label: Preparations for electricity imports
sections.summary: Suitable subsea cable routes and landing sites for imports from Indonesia are identified, and a feasibility study on a second Malaysia interconnector is being conducted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: To prepare for imports from Indonesia, we have identified suitable subsea cable connection routes and landing sites.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are also conducting a full feasibility study on a second interconnector between Singapore and Malaysia.

sections.label: Biomethane explored through regulatory sandbox
sections.summary: Biomethane is being explored as a viable low-carbon fuel through a regulatory sandbox of up to 300 megawatts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: First, we are exploring biomethane as a viable low-carbon fuel through a regulatory sandbox of up to 300 megawatts (MW).

sections.label: Advanced nuclear energy technologies studied
sections.summary: No decision has been made, but advanced nuclear energy technologies such as small modular reactors are being seriously studied.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Other low-carbon solutions are not yet ready for deployment at scale, either due to technological nascency or under-developed supply chains.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Thus, while we have not made a decision – and let me reiterate this, we have not made a decision – we are seriously studying the potential deployment of advanced nuclear energy technologies, such as small modular reactors.

sections.label: Decarbonisation Grand Challenge funding
sections.summary: A new $800 million Decarbonisation Grand Challenge is launched under RIE2030 to support 2035 abatement targets and 2050 net-zero ambitions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Underpinning all these efforts is science and technology as the key enabler.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are launching a new $800 million Decarbonisation Grand Challenge under RIE2030, in support of our 2035 abatement targets and 2050 net-zero ambitions.

sections.label: Business Refresh Package for enterprises
sections.summary: The Government has tailored a Business Refresh Package of enhancements to existing schemes to help enterprises stay resilient, grow and thrive.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I want to assure them that the Government is leaving no stone unturned to support and to journey alongside our enterprises as they adapt, transform and innovate to overcome the challenges faced.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that the Government has tailored a "Business Refresh Package" that comprises a suite of enhancements to existing schemes, to enable, equip and empower our enterprises at every step of their journey to stay resilient, grow and thrive by: one, enhancing their productivity and cost efficiency; two, growing their revenue and helping them capture fresh opportunities at home and abroad; and three, fostering a pro-enterprise and trusted business environment.

sections.label: Frosts automated storage system results
sections.summary: Frosts, with COI-SCM, rolled out a four-way shuttle automated storage and retrieval system at its Bedok facility, yielding over 30% manpower efficiency gains and about $100,000 annual savings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In partnership with COI-SCM, Frosts conceptualised and rolled out a four-way shuttle automated storage and retrieval system at its Bedok facility.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This has led to manpower efficiency improvements of over 30% and approximately $100,000 in annual cost savings for the company.

sections.label: EFS-Green extension
sections.summary: In 2024 the EFS-Green was extended two years and expanded to cover companies adopting green solutions, and it will be extended another five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In 2024, we extended the Enterprise Financing Scheme (EFS)-Green for two years and expanded the scope to cover companies adopting green solutions, in addition to green technology developers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We will extend the EFS-Green for another five years.

sections.label: Removing EFS facility-level sub-caps
sections.summary: Facility-level sub-caps of $20 million and $30 million per borrower group for EFS-Trade Loan and EFS-Fixed Assets Loan will be removed, retaining the $50 million overall cap.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To allow lenders greater flexibility in structuring loan facilities, we will remove the facility-level sub-caps of $20 million and $30 million per borrower group for the EFS-Trade Loan and the EFS-Fixed Assets Loan respectively, while retaining the overall cap of $50 million.

sections.label: Higher grants for venturing abroad
sections.summary: Support levels for grant schemes helping businesses venture abroad will rise from 50% to 70% for SMEs and 30% to 50% for non-SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: First, we will increase the support levels for grant schemes that help businesses venture abroad, from 50% to 70% for SMEs, and 30% to 50% for non-SMEs.

sections.label: Grant cap extension for local businesses
sections.summary: The $100,000 grant cap is extended, new markets criteria removed, and grant support extended to all local businesses including SMEs and non-SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Members will remember at MTI's COS debate last year, I announced an extension of the $100,000 grant cap to 31 March 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This year, in addition to extending the $100,000 grant cap, we will remove new markets criteria and will extend grant support to all local businesses, including both SMEs and non-SMEs.

sections.label: Higher cap for automatic deductions
sections.summary: The expenditure cap for automatic DTDi-qualifying activities rises from $150,000 to $400,000, and existing qualifying activities become eligible for automatic deductions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To help the companies seize overseas opportunities with greater speed and certainty, we will increase the expenditure cap for automatic DTDi-qualifying activities from $150,000 to $400,000 and make existing qualifying activities eligible for automatic deductions.

sections.label: Enhanced support for heartland schemes
sections.summary: Support levels for the Enhanced Visual Merchandising Programme and Heartland Enterprise Placemaking Grant increase from 50% to 70%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To encourage the rejuvenation of our heartland shops, we will enhance the support levels of our heartland schemes, the Enhanced Visual Merchandising Programme and the Heartland Enterprise Placemaking Grant, from 50% to 70%.

sections.label: New EDGE grant single shopfront
sections.summary: A new EDGE grant provides a single shopfront for Government grants, merging the MRA grant, PSG and EDG, supporting up to $100,000 per year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Beyond enhancing enterprise support, the Government will streamline grant processes to make it easier for our businesses to access the full suite of available measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce a new grant, EDGE, which will provide a single shopfront for Government grants, merging the MRA grant, PSG and EDG.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The new EDGE grant will support up to $100,000 per year for eligible activities.

sections.label: EDGE launch by Enterprise Singapore
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore will launch EDGE in the second half of 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Enterprise Singapore will launch EDGE in the second half of 2026.

sections.label: Service standards for regulatory applications
sections.summary: Agencies published service standards for 93% of business regulatory applications, with 80% processed within 30 working days.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: First, to publish clear service standards for regulatory applications, with a target of 30 working days where possible.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that agencies have published service standards for 93% of their business regulatory applications, with 80% of these applications processed within 30 working days.

sections.label: Consumer protection review panel
sections.summary: CCS has sought Court injunctions against egregious businesses, and an independent Consumer Protection Review Panel convened in March last year will recommend on consumer concerns.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Where necessary, CCS has sought Court injunctions against egregious businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: MTI and CCS will certainly consider this, as part of the Government's regular review of the remedies under the CPFTA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To ensure that our consumer protection regime is up to date, the Government convened an independent Consumer Protection Review Panel last year in March.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The Panel will put forward recommendations to address key consumer concerns, including pressure sales tactics and emerging digital harms, such as undisclosed advertisements.

sections.label: Tourism arrivals and receipts
sections.summary: Last year Singapore welcomed 16.9 million international visitors, up 2.3%, and tourism receipts reached $23.9 billion in the first three quarters of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Last year, we welcomed 16.9 million international visitors, a 2.3% increase from 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Importantly, our tourism receipts reached $23.9 billion in the first three quarters of 2025, a 6.5% increase compared to the same period in 2024.

sections.label: Expected visitor arrivals and receipts
sections.summary: International visitor arrivals are expected to reach between 17 million and 18 million this year, bringing in approximately $31 billion to $32.5 billion in tourism receipts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Building on this momentum, we expect international visitor arrivals to reach between 17 million and 18 million this year, bringing in approximately $31 billion to $32.5 billion in tourism receipts.

sections.label: Marina Bay cruise centre capacity
sections.summary: In October, Marina Bay Cruise Centre Singapore's capacity was increased from 6,800 to 11,700 passengers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In October, we increased Marina Bay Cruise Centre Singapore's capacity, from 6,800 to 11,700 passengers.

sections.label: Venture capital funding growth
sections.summary: Venture capital funding to startups more than quadrupled in the past decade, from US$1 billion in 2014 to US$4.8 billion in 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Venture capital (VC) funding to startups more than quadrupled in the past decade, from US$1 billion in 2014 to US$4.8 billion in 2024.

sections.label: Startup SG Equity expansion funding
sections.summary: $1 billion will be set aside to expand the Startup SG Equity (SSGE) scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: First, we will set aside $1 billion to expand the Startup SG Equity (SSGE) scheme.

sections.label: Anchor Fund second tranche
sections.summary: The bulk of the fund was deployed to support companies seeking public listing in Singapore, and a second $1.5 billion tranche, Anchor Fund 2, will now launch.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We have deployed the bulk of this fund to support companies in their journey towards public listing in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We will now launch the second $1.5 billion tranche of the Anchor Fund, or Anchor Fund 2.

sections.label: Dual listing and private capital
sections.summary: An SGX-Nasdaq dual listing bridge will let eligible companies list on both exchanges with one prospectus, and a workgroup will develop strategies for growth capital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Our upcoming SGX-Nasdaq dual listing bridge will also allow eligible companies to simultaneously list on both exchanges with one set of prospectus.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: But we recognise that not every company will want to raise capital through our public markets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We must thus help our startups better access private capital to meet their diverse financing needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Minister Chee Hong Tat has convened a new workgroup to develop strategies to strengthen Singapore as a leading centre for growth capital.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We have met the workgroup and look forward to developing measures to better help our companies raise private capital and pursue other non-public exits.

sections.label: LaunchPad startup support
sections.summary: Since JTC repurposed Block 71 Ayer Rajah Crescent and expanded the startup hub in 2015, LaunchPad @ One-North has supported over 2,400 startups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: Since JTC repurposed Block 71 Ayer Rajah Crescent and expanded the startup hub in 2015, LaunchPad @ One-North has supported over 2,400 startups, including tech unicorns Carousell, PatSnap and Nium.

sections.label: LaunchPad extension and refresh
sections.summary: JTC will extend and refresh LaunchPad to create more space for next-gen startups, making it Asia's flagship startup destination.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: To create more space for next-gen startups such as those in Lorong AI, JTC will extend and refresh LaunchPad, making it Asia's flagship startup destination.

sections.label: Kampong AI park
sections.summary: A key highlight of the refresh is a new AI park called Kampong AI.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: A key highlight of the refresh, as mentioned in the Prime Minister's Budget speech, is a new AI park called "Kampong AI".

sections.label: Kampong AI in 2028
sections.summary: When ready in 2028, Kampong AI will be the place for AI startups and talent to congregate and exchange ideas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Ms Gan Siow Huang)
sentences.text: When ready in 2028, Kampong AI will be the place for AI startups and talent to congregate and exchange ideas.

sections.label: Space for AI community
sections.summary: It says a space is crucial for AI leaders and practitioners, comprising two seven-storey developments with business park units and event spaces for around 70 companies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: It is crucial for our budding community of AI leaders and practitioners to have a space to share ideas and build new products.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: It comprises two adjacent seven-storey developments – one block with 14,500 square metres of business park units and event spaces accommodating around 70 companies.

sections.label: Pilot workspaces from 2026
sections.summary: It states that while fully ready by 2028, pilot workspaces will be available in LaunchPad @ One-North from 2026 for firms wanting a headstart.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: While only fully ready by 2028, pilot workspaces will be available in LaunchPad @ One-North from 2026 onwards for firms that want a headstart.

sections.label: Woodlands Gateway district plan
sections.summary: It states JTC is master-planning a Woodlands Gateway district around the RTS Link station, with a first phase expected around 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: JTC is master-planning an exciting new Woodlands Gateway district around the upcoming Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link station, which will be our northern gateway to the Johor-Singapore SEZ.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: This mixed-use district, spanning up to 35-hectares, that is about the size of 50 football fields, will include a transport hub connected to the RTS Link and Woodlands North MRT stations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: The first phase is expected to complete around 2030.

sections.label: ASEAN agreements upgraded
sections.summary: It states ASEAN upgraded the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement and ASEAN-China Free Trade Area 3.0, and concluded the Digital Economy Framework Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Last year, ASEAN upgraded two landmark agreements which are used extensively by our traders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: These are the ASEAN Trade in Goods Agreement and ASEAN-China Free Trade Area 3.0.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We also concluded the Digital Economy Framework Agreement to work towards a single and trusted regional digital ecosystem.

sections.label: Digital Economy Partnership Agreement expansion
sections.summary: It states participation in the Digital Economic Partnership Agreement is expanding, with Costa Rica and Peru joining and China and the UAE in accession discussions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We are expanding participation in the Digital Economic Partnership Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: It will soon grow to six members with Costa Rica and Peru joining later this year, while China and the UAE are in accession discussions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Lastly, we are actively strengthening our economic security through close collaboration with trusted partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: We are finalising a first-of-its-kind Agreement on Trade in Essential Supplies with New Zealand.

sections.label: Questions on support and energy
sections.summary: It asks whether MTI has defined trigger conditions for targeted support and whether development expenditure numbers include energy infrastructure plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: My related question is on enterprise support in that segment is, whether the Deputy Prime Minister can clarify whether MTI has defined clear trigger conditions, such as sustained increases in energy costs or trade disruptions, under which targeted and timebound support will be activated?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Second is on our plans to budget for physical energy infrastructure to meet our energy resilience and strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: I note in MOF's Budget documents that our development expenditure for MTI has increased from about $4.92 billion in FY2025 to $9.24 billion, an increase of about $4.3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: Can I ask Minister Tan or Deputy Prime Minister whether the numbers already include some of our plans for energy infrastructure to meet some of the energy resilience and strategy, including, for example, landing points, energy storage and whatever new alternative energy that we are taking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
sentences.text: My question is, I embedded in my speech, what is the projected economic contribution and job creation from the Greater Sentosa Master Plan besides the transport connection between Sentosa and Brani, how many jobs will be created and how many percent value added into GDP will it add to?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: First, let me address the issue on our outlook for our economy and inflation as a result of the various scenarios that Mr Saktiandi has pointed out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I think tariffs have a significant impact on Singapore, not just the direct tariff between Singapore and the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But what is even more important is the environment under which we are now operating, where tariffs can be adjusted at will, and with very short notice, overnight.

sections.label: Strait of Hormuz shipping route
sections.summary: The Strait of Hormuz is a key shipping route for energy, LNG and oil.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: What we need to bear in mind is that the Strait of Hormuz is a key shipping route for energy, for LNG, for oil.

sections.label: MTI budget incremental delta
sections.summary: The MTI budget's incremental delta considers different aspects of increased spending, including the $800 million Decarbonisation Grand Challenge.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the short answer to Mr Saktiandi's clarification on the incremental delta for the MTI budget does take into consideration different aspects of the increased spending.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I have alluded to the Decarbonisation Grand Challenge of $800 million.

sections.label: Greater Sentosa Master Plan Phase One
sections.summary: Greater Sentosa Master Plan Phase One is expected to attract about 5.3 million international visitor arrivals in 2045.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: Sentosa is just one part – a very important part, of course – of our overall Tourism Strategy 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: We expect tourism receipts to reach about $47 billion to $50 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: With respect to the Greater Sentosa Master Plan Phase One, which I mentioned earlier, once it has been completed, Greater Sentosa is expected to attract approximately 5.3 million international visitor arrivals in 2045.

sections.label: Assessing R&D economic outcomes
sections.summary: The member asks how the Government assesses economic outcomes of R&D and commercialisation of public-funded IP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: Chairman, I have spoken earlier about how Singapore and our businesses cannot compete on costs alone but must continue to focus on innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee
sentences.text: As such, I would like to ask Minister Tan to share how the Government assess the economic outcomes of our R&D and the commercialisation of public-funded IP, in terms of enterprise formation, licensing to local firms, contribution to GDP and higher value jobs.

sections.label: Business R&D expenditure growth
sections.summary: From 2016 to 2023 annual business R&D expenditure grew 7.8% yearly to $9 billion, with private investment per public dollar rising to $1.87.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: If we look at over an eight- to nine-year horizon, from 2016 to 2023, the total annual business expenditure on R&D grew by a compound annual growth rate of 7.8%, reaching $9 billion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, in 2023, every $1 spent by the public sector on R&D saw $1.87 correspondingly invested by the private sector, and this is up from the $1.38 in 2016.

sections.label: Private sector R&D jobs growth
sections.summary: Between 2016 and 2023 private sector R&D jobs grew 36% to more than 30,000, with locals filling over 70%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Between 2016 and 2023, R&D jobs in the private sector grew by 36%, reaching more than 30,000, with locals filling more than 70% of these roles.

sections.label: A*STAR and IHL spinoffs
sections.summary: In five years, A*STAR and IHLs spun off over 300 companies and awarded over 900 licences to SMEs and startups.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Just the last five years alone, A*STAR and our IHLs' technologies have spun off more than 300 new companies, 230 local SMEs and startups have also licensed some 300 A*STAR originated technologies, while over 900 licences were awarded by our IHLs to SMEs and startups.

sections.label: Johor-Singapore SEZ and Digital Nomad Pass
sections.summary: Singapore will facilitate a Johor-Singapore SEZ industrial estate and is exploring a Digital Nomad Pass with Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Victor Lye for his clarifications on the idea of a Singapore industrial estate in the Johor-Singapore SEZ.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: It is an interesting idea and we will be happy to facilitate if there are interested commercial parties that are willing to invest in this estate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: On creating arrangements for people to be able to live in the SEZ and be able to work seamlessly in both places, we are exploring a Digital Nomad Pass between the Singapore Government and the Malaysian government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: And just for your information today, Malaysia already has an existing Digital Nomad Pass, which allows foreigners to reside in Malaysia without being employed there.

sentences.speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
sentences.text: So, there is already something that we can leverage and we are looking at enhancing it further.

sections.label: Ammonia and hydrogen FEED studies
sections.summary: FEED studies with a local conglomerate look at ammonia as a pathway, alongside hydrogen, both well-understood molecules.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To the first point, indeed, as I have alluded to just now on the ammonia study that we have proceeded with, we have actually worked with a local conglomerate where we have moved on to do FEED studies, where not only do we look at ammonia as one possible pathway – and I will tell you why we look at ammonia; I know the Member was talking about hydrogen – because ammonia as a molecule, hydrogen as a molecule, they are both quite well understood.

sections.label: Sandboxes and Decarbonisation Grand Challenge
sections.summary: Bigger sandboxes encourage gencos and large companies to work with local SMEs, as does the $800 million Decarbonisation Grand Challenge.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: For many of these bigger sandboxes, we encourage – whether it is the generating companies (gencos), whether it is large companies – to work locally with our SMEs as well to bring them along.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And the point that I alluded to earlier on, on the $800 million Decarbonisation Grand Challenge, is something that we hope to be able to crowd in from the big gencos, the big MNCs, to our local SMEs to bring them along in helping us to decarbonise.

sections.label: Low carbon importers and data centres
sections.summary: Low carbon importers can strike commercial arrangements with big energy intake customers like Google and Amazon Web Services, ring-fenced.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, where we come in is, we try to allow for the low carbon importers to strike up commercial arrangements with the big energy intake customers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, the likes of, whether it is Google, Amazon Web Services, some of these data centres, we allow them to negotiate and we ring-fence it.

sections.label: Natural gas decarbonisation costs and carbon pricing
sections.summary: Carbon pricing reflects the true cost of natural gas generation, including capturing, aggregating, transporting and storing emissions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And for the longer term, as we move on to decarbonisation, notwithstanding the fact that the natural gas will always be our base, we are, indeed, mindful of the cost of continuing with natural gas, then you have to add the cost of decarbonising that natural gas, the emissions you have to capture – you have to aggregate it, you have to transport it, then you have to store it – these also come with costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, our carbon pricing is a reflection of the true cost of that particular modality of energy generation.

sections.label: Support for SMEs and micro enterprises
sections.summary: Government will increase support intensity, expand support scope and simplify application processes so SMEs and micro enterprises get support faster.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, we will make two important adjustments: increasing our support intensity and expanding the scope of support to help our enterprises seize growth opportunities and expand their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: We will integrate and simplify application processes so that SMEs, including micro enterprises, can obtain Government support more quickly and easily, enabling them to focus their energy on business innovation and future development.

sections.label: Developing leadership in MNCs and sectors
sections.summary: One way to deepen leadership is to develop leadership in MNCs, companies and sectors with a strong foundation, such as semiconductors and pharmaceuticals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: First, I think one of the ways to deepen our leadership and to strengthen our depth is to develop leadership in our MNCs, in our companies, in our sectors where we already have a strong foundation, like semiconductors, pharmaceuticals and so on.

sections.label: Attracting R&D functions to Singapore
sections.summary: The aim is to attract key operation functions, including R&D, so companies build R&D facilities and capabilities in Singapore instead of elsewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And by doing so, we also want to attract key operation functions here, including R&D.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, instead of doing R&D elsewhere, we want to encourage them to bring the R&D facilities here, build the R&D capabilities in Singapore.

sections.label: Digitalisation, AI and TAC partnerships
sections.summary: Working with Enterprise Singapore and JTC, digitalisation and AI raised production capacity six times; Enterprise Singapore and MTI will continue working with TACs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: — they have been working very closely with Enterprise Singapore and JTC, and in one stroke, because of them onboarding digitalisation transformation and as well as AI, they have managed to increase their production capacity by not just double or triple, but six times.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: On TACs, Enterprise Singapore and MTI will continue to work very closely with our range of TACs, including SBF, SCCCI, SMCCI, SICCI and so on.

sections.label: Consumer protection review and regime
sections.summary: Government convened an independent Consumer Protection Review Panel last year and stands prepared to take a whole-of-Government view to enhance consumer protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: You would have heard in my earlier speech, I shared that the Government convened an independent Consumer Protection Review Panel last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: We will take a very thorough look at some of that because some of the feedback from the focus group discussions actually cover the areas the Member talked about.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: I want to assure him that it is not just CCS, not just the MTI family, but we stand prepared to take a whole-of-Government view to enhance our consumer protection regime to do two things.
